no_block_assessment: For this mechanic set, `nothing is blocked` can safely mean that a valid deck package may still reach `technical_status=VALID_PACKAGE` and `runtime_apply_mode=load_safe_apply` even when some mechanics are only partially represented or remain warning-only. That is the correct contract for a pre-run generator and should not be confused with full strategic completeness.

Directly lowerable means HSConfig has a documented normal-path row for the mechanic's core action. In the requested set that is true today for Battlecry, Overload, Weapons, and Discard. Those mechanics already map to documented CardID or Combo surfaces without needing speculative identity inference.

Identity-gated-direct means HSConfig can lower the mechanic only when exact option or transformed identity is proven. In the requested set that applies to Discover and Hero Power swaps. They are lowerable through `OnDiscoverCardBonus` or `BeforeUseHeroPowerBonus`, but unresolved option identity must stay suppressed.

Partial means HSConfig can lower real pre-run posture or timing value for the mechanic, but not the full signature action tree. In the requested set that applies to Deathrattle, Reborn, Recruit, Freeze, Lifesteal, Taunt, Rush, Charge, Locations, Secrets, generated entities, aura, Destroy, Silence, Transform, and Imbue.

Warning-only means HSConfig should name the mechanic in visibility reports but must not invent a runtime row for its defining action. In the requested set that applies to positioning, Dredge, Tradeable, Kindred, Tourist, Starship, Rewind, Herald, and Shatter. This is a deliberate safety boundary, not missing engineering hygiene.

Unknown-warning is the fallback for future unregistered mechanics or card-role drift. It is still needed as a class of behavior, but it is not the right label for any of the named mechanics in this specific audit because all requested mechanics are now explicitly registered.
hearthstone_semantic_coverage: Directly lowerable today: Battlecry, Overload, Weapons, and Discard. Repo truth is `support_level=direct`, and their normal-path surfaces are already explicit: Battlecry uses `BeforeBattlecryTargetBonus` or `BeforePlayCardBonus` and can participate in `Combo.json`; Overload lowers through `BeforePlayCardBonus` plus deck-posture GlobalValues; Weapons lower through `BeforePhysicalAttackBonus`, `BeforePlayCardBonus`, and exact weapon-sequence combo rows; Discard lowers through `BeforePlayCardBonus` for the enabler timing.

Identity-gated-direct today: Discover and Hero Power swaps. Discover is visible as `identity_gated_direct` because the mechanic can lower through `OnDiscoverCardBonus`, but unresolved option identity must stay suppressed. Hero Power swaps map to `hero_power_transform`, are also `identity_gated_direct`, and remain exact-identity dependent because current HearthstoneJSON still does not provide a universally rich linked-entity layer by itself.

Partial today: Deathrattle, Reborn, Recruit, Freeze, Lifesteal, Taunt, Rush, Charge, Locations, Secrets, generated entities, aura, Destroy, Silence, Transform, and Imbue. These mechanics are real pre-run semantics in HSConfig, but the lowering is intentionally limited to deploy posture, attack posture, board posture, survivability posture, or exact resolved identities where those are documented.

Deathrattle, Reborn, and Recruit are partial because HSConfig can time the source card or encourage board posture, but it does not claim exact trigger ordering, resurrection quality, or recruited pull identity from runtime rows alone. The same-day collectible probe still shows all three mechanics are active in live card data, so keeping them named as partial is better than flattening them into generic value text.

Freeze, Lifesteal, Taunt, Rush, Charge, Destroy, Silence, and Transform are partial because they have real combat or play-timing meaning, but exact trade math, target selection, frozen-state checks, or transform outcomes remain broader runtime evaluation instead of safe static lowering. This is the right pre-run boundary for a lean generator.

Locations and Secrets split into a partial core mechanic plus a warning-only sub-boundary for the hidden or repeated-action parts. `location` is partial for play timing, while `location_activation` stays report-only; `secret` is partial for play timing or mulligan posture, while `secret_timing` remains report-only because hidden-information sequencing is not a documented normal-path row.

Generated entities and aura stay partial for the same reason: exact resolved identities can sometimes lower, but random pools and continuous board-state math cannot. The operator contract is explicit that `generated_entity_random_pool` is warning-only, which keeps random generation honest without hiding the mechanic entirely.

Warning-only today: positioning, Dredge, Tradeable, Kindred, Tourist, Starship, Rewind, Herald, and Shatter. Positioning has no documented VisionAI placement row; Dredge and Tradeable are choice-before-play decisions without a safe normal-path choice surface; Kindred depends on previous-turn type or school state; Tourist is deck-construction identity rather than an in-game action row; Starship depends on build and launch state; Rewind depends on prior-state replay; Herald depends on card-specific Colossal scaling; and Shatter depends on conditional frozen-target semantics.

Current card-data drift matters here. The same-day collectible probe found Kindred on 30 texts, Tourist on 13, Starship on 38 texts plus 38 referenced-tag hits, Imbue on 19, Rewind on 20, Herald on 15, and Shatter on 7. These mechanics are therefore current enough that explicit warning-only or partial registration is better than relying on unnamed fallback behavior.

Current unknown-warning count for the requested list is zero. That is the strongest positive change relative to earlier drift waves: Rewind, Herald, and Shatter no longer need to be treated as unnamed future drift. They are now explicitly named `warning_only`, which is safer for operators and more honest than pretending they are lowerable.
provided_deck_matrix_assessment: The provided 11 representative decks plus supplemental CuteWarrior are still enough proof for the any-valid-deck load-safe package claim, because the no-block promise is about technical package validity and safe runtime shape, not about proving a first-class runtime lane for every live mechanic.

The current matrix still covers the high-value Wild families that matter most for pre-run package competence: Battlecry and Hero Power swap pressure in ShadowPriest and ImbueMage, Recruit in CtAPaladin and BigShaman, Weapon sequencing in Kingslayer and PirateRogue, Discard in Discolock, combo sequencing in Boarlock, board or aura snowball in TreantDruid and MechPala, and aggressive attack posture in PirateDH and CuteWarrior.

The matrix does not directly deck-prove every requested warning-only family. There is no dedicated representative row for Dredge, Tradeable, Kindred, Tourist, Starship, Rewind, Herald, or Shatter. That is acceptable because those mechanics are intentionally non-blocking and mostly report-only rather than candidates for richer runtime write permission.

The matrix is thinner for Discover-control, Freeze-control, Location-heavy, and Secret-heavy shells than it is for Recruit, Weapon, Discard, or Hero Power shells. That is a richness gap, not an any-deck load-safe blocker, because the repo contract and tests already keep those mechanics inside explicit identity-gated, partial, or warning-only boundaries.

Expanding the matrix just to prove warning-only mechanics would add maintenance cost without changing the actual recommendation. For this audit, the current deck set is adequate because the missing mechanics are missing from rich proof, not from the safety contract.
skill_slimness_assessment: The current HSConfig design stays slim because it separates runtime permission from semantic richness. Direct, identity-gated, partial, warning-only, and unknown-warning are explanation buckets, not new apply gates.

Naming Rewind, Herald, and Shatter as registered warning-only mechanics is a slim improvement, not scope creep. It improves operator truth without inventing extra runtime rows, extra HSTuner behavior, or post-run evaluation logic.

Keeping Dredge, Tradeable, Positioning, Kindred, Tourist, Starship, Rewind, Herald, and Shatter warning-only is the right lean choice. The alternative would be fabricated lowering that looks richer than the documented VisionAI surfaces actually are.

The registry-driven approach is materially better than deck-sprawl as a way to handle future Wild drift. One explicit support row plus one drift test is cheaper and clearer than adding new representative decks every time Blizzard prints another mechanic keyword.

The current boundary still respects the intended product: a narrow, pre-run config generator that emits safe loadable packages and honest reports, not a full strategic simulator or runtime policy engine.
gaps_or_risks: Latest HearthstoneJSON still exposes `entourage=0` rows and `playRequirements=0` rows on 2026-07-10, so exact generated-pool closure, exact targeting constraints, and some option-link edges still need supplemental deterministic logic or warning-only handling rather than broader lowering claims.

Current latest `cards.json` also contains mode-specific or non-normal card types such as `battleground_anomaly`, `battleground_spell`, `battleground_trinket`, `battleground_hero_buddy`, `lettuce_ability`, `pet`, `game_mode_button`, and `move_minion_hover_target`. That drift is harmless today because HSConfig scopes mechanic analysis to deck-card payloads, but it would become noisy if future audits stopped filtering to deck-relevant cards.

Some live text markers are semantically overloaded. Simple text hits for generated-entity or aura-style effects can overcount broad card-text patterns if used as exact mechanic totals. They are good drift indicators, not exact strategic coverage proofs.

The representative deck matrix remains lighter on Discover-control, Freeze-control, Secret-heavy, and Location-heavy proof than on Weapon, Recruit, Discard, or combo shells. That is acceptable for no-block safety, but it means some partial and identity-gated mechanics are currently proven more by registry and tests than by deck-fixture variety.
recommended_next_action: No immediate code change is required. The best next action is to keep the current registry-driven boundary and only refresh the live keyword probe after each new Hearthstone expansion or mini-set, adding a new explicit support row only when a newly live mechanic is not already covered by the existing direct, identity-gated, partial, or warning-only buckets.
